---
title: "Other uses of alternative data beyond CPI"
date-modified: "2026-05-12"
---

Beyond CPI production, many of the data sources and processes described
in this handbook may also support a range of other official statistical
domains.

In many cases, early consideration of cross-domain needs can help reduce
duplication of data acquisition and processing efforts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Price statistics beyond CPI {#OtherusesofalternativedatabeyondCPI-PricestatisticsbeyondCPI end="1026" data-start="988"}

Alternative data sources can support several price-related statistical
outputs beyond the CPI, including:

- Purchasing Power Parities (PPPs), where detailed price information for
  comparable products and services is required across countries

- Producer Price Indices (PPIs) and other business price indices,
  particularly for retail, wholesale, and selected service activities

- Export and Import Price Indices, where transaction-level or
  invoice-based data may be available

- residential property and rental price statistics, where web-scraped
  listings and administrative records are increasingly used

# National accounts and macroeconomic statistics {#OtherusesofalternativedatabeyondCPI-Nationalaccountsandmacroeconomicstatistics end="1424" data-start="1374" style="text-align: left;"}

Transaction and administrative data can contribute to national accounts
compilation, particularly where they provide detailed information on
prices, quantities, or turnover. Relevant areas include:

- household final consumption expenditure, including detailed
  product-level breakdowns

- deflators used to derive volume measures in national accounts

- supply-use tables, where consistent price and quantity information
  supports balancing

- short-term indicators, such as monthly or quarterly estimates of
  consumption or turnover

# Business and structural statistics {#OtherusesofalternativedatabeyondCPI-Businessandstructuralstatistics end="2014" data-start="1976" style="text-align: left;"}

Alternative data sources may also support business-focused statistical
domains, including:

- retail and wholesale trade statistics, using turnover and quantity
  data

- structural business statistics, where administrative or transaction
  data can supplement or replace surveys

- business demography and firm dynamics, through transaction records and
  administrative datasets

- service sector statistics, particularly for digitally delivered
  services and platforms

# Household and distributional statistics {#OtherusesofalternativedatabeyondCPI-Householdanddistributionalstatistics end="2541" data-start="2498" style="text-align: left;"}

Where access and legal frameworks permit, alternative data sources may
support more granular analysis of household behaviour, including:

- consumption patterns and expenditure distributions, when combined with
  other sources

- experimental distributional measures, subject to confidentiality
  constraints

- analysis of substitution behaviour and market dynamics, particularly
  during periods of rapid change

# Emerging and cross-cutting statistical domains {#OtherusesofalternativedatabeyondCPI-Emergingandcross-cuttingstatisticaldomains end="3015" data-start="2965" style="text-align: left;"}

In some cases, alternative data sources may support newer or
cross-cutting statistical needs, such as:

- digital economy and platform statistics, including e-commerce and
  digital services

- environmental and sustainability statistics, where transaction data
  can support consumption-based analyses

- experimental statistics and research outputs, particularly where
  timeliness or granularity is prioritised

- nowcasting for Central Banks / other forecasting organisations

While conceptual and methodological requirements can differ across
statistical domains, many processing steps such as data cleaning,
product identification, and temporal aggregation are common. Early
consideration of potential reuse can therefore support more efficient
and coherent use of alternative data across statistical systems.
